# Leading engineering teams

English · [Русский](../ru/themes/engineering-leadership.md) · ← [AI Interview Atlas](../../README.md)

Hiring, coaching, performance, team design and delivery for teams that build AI.

## Both tracks

- **Describe how you identified a valuable opportunity and persuaded a group to deliver it.**
  - Behavioral · Senior · Asked at: [Monzo](../companies/monzo.md) ✅
  - Tests: Whether you create influence through evidence, alignment and shared ownership.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Explain why the opportunity mattered and how you discovered it.
    - Describe competing priorities, objections and how participants shaped the plan.
    - Show delivery and impact, including what remained outside your control.
  - Read: [Design Docs at Google](https://www.industrialempathy.com/posts/design-docs-at-google/) (Industrial Empathy) · [Site Reliability Engineering](https://sre.google/sre-book/table-of-contents/) (Google)

## AI Leadership

- **Tell me how you handled an engineer who was not meeting expectations.**
  - Behavioral · Senior · Asked at: [Google and Google DeepMind](../companies/google.md) 🗣
  - Tests: Whether you diagnose performance fairly and make expectations actionable.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Identify the performance gap using observable examples.
    - Explain the feedback, listening and support you provided.
    - Describe agreed next steps and the follow-up result.
  - Read: [[re:Work] Google's New Manager Training Slides](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/13-rj7ZqlyuHNli9Ybd5D8g-qqUNtG81t3JLq7JV5c2o/htmlpresent) (Google re:Work)
- **How did you handle a high-performing engineer whose behaviour caused conflict with colleagues?**
  - Behavioral · Senior · Asked at: [Google and Google DeepMind](../companies/google.md) 🗣
  - Tests: Whether you hold performance and collaboration to explicit standards.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Separate technical results from the impact of specific behaviour.
    - Explain your feedback and how you heard their perspective.
    - Describe agreed behaviour changes and subsequent observations.
  - Read: [[re:Work] Google's New Manager Training Slides](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/13-rj7ZqlyuHNli9Ybd5D8g-qqUNtG81t3JLq7JV5c2o/htmlpresent) (Google re:Work)
- **Describe how someone you mentored progressed in their career.**
  - Behavioral · Senior · Asked at: [Anthropic](../companies/anthropic.md) 🗣
  - Tests: Whether you develop others through opportunities and evidence rather than taking credit for their success.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Describe their development goal and starting point.
    - Explain how coaching helped them choose actions.
    - Distinguish their achievements from your support.
  - Read: [[re:Work] Google's New Manager Training Slides](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/13-rj7ZqlyuHNli9Ybd5D8g-qqUNtG81t3JLq7JV5c2o/htmlpresent) (Google re:Work)
- **What do you do when your team disagrees with your proposed direction?**
  - Applied scenario · Senior · Asked at: [Anthropic](../companies/anthropic.md) 🗣
  - Tests: Whether you invite challenge while retaining responsibility for a decision.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Clarify the disputed assumptions and actively seek the strongest objection.
    - Use evidence or a bounded experiment where it can resolve the disagreement.
    - Explain decision rights, communicate the choice and define when to revisit it.
  - Read: [Design Docs at Google](https://www.industrialempathy.com/posts/design-docs-at-google/) (Industrial Empathy)
- **How would you respond when a high performer considers leaving during a reorganisation?**
  - Applied scenario · Senior · Asked at: [Google and Google DeepMind](../companies/google.md) 🗣
  - Tests: Whether you listen honestly and address retention without making promises you cannot keep.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Understand the person's concerns and separate change uncertainty from persistent problems.
    - Explain what is known, what you can change and what remains undecided.
    - Discuss feasible support, surface unresolved concerns and agree a follow-up.
  - Read: [Organizational Change Management](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/organizational-change-management/) (GitLab Handbook)
- **How would you stabilise an engineering team after a change in management?**
  - Applied scenario · Senior · Asked at: [Google and Google DeepMind](../companies/google.md) 🗣
  - Tests: Whether you establish trust and operating clarity before imposing broad changes.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Listen to team members and partners and identify urgent delivery or wellbeing risks.
    - Clarify priorities, decision ownership and communication routines.
    - Make a small number of justified changes and check their effect.
  - Read: [Organizational Change Management](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/organizational-change-management/) (GitLab Handbook)
- **What is the largest team you have managed, and how did your responsibilities change at that scale?**
  - Self-presentation · Senior · Asked at: [Anthropic](../companies/anthropic.md) 🗣
  - Tests: Whether your management model matches the actual span and complexity.
- **How have you managed and developed your strongest performers?**
  - Behavioral · Senior · Asked at: [Meta](../companies/meta.md) 🗣
  - Tests: Whether you provide challenge and growth without creating a privileged exception.
- **A cross-functional partner gives you critical feedback about your leadership. How do you respond?**
  - Applied scenario · Senior · Asked at: [Meta](../companies/meta.md) 🗣
  - Tests: Whether you investigate feedback and translate it into changed behaviour.
- **Describe a team disagreement that you resolved without discarding the valid concerns on either side.**
  - Behavioral · Senior · Asked at: [Google and Google DeepMind](../companies/google.md) 🗣
  - Tests: Whether you uncover underlying needs instead of forcing a superficial compromise.
- **How do you decide which engineering capabilities to hire for?**
  - Applied scenario · Senior · Asked at: [Stripe](../companies/stripe.md) †
  - Tests: Whether staffing choices follow strategy and gaps in team capability.
- **How do you establish engineering quality standards across a team?**
  - Applied scenario · Senior · Asked at: [Stripe](../companies/stripe.md) †
  - Tests: Whether standards are observable, proportionate and part of daily delivery.
- **How would you convince engineers that a proposed product feature is worth building?**
  - Applied scenario · Senior · Asked at: [Perplexity](../companies/perplexity.md) †
  - Tests: Whether you engage technical concerns and establish a shared reason to invest.
- **What have you changed about your management approach as you have grown?**
  - Behavioral · Senior · Asked at: [Meta](../companies/meta.md) 🗣
  - Tests: Whether reflection produces concrete changes in how you lead.
- **Researchers want more exploration while product engineers need a reliable release. How would you structure ownership and handoffs?**
  - Applied scenario · Senior · 🧪 generated from job-posting themes
  - Tests: Whether team design accommodates uncertainty without abandoning production ownership.
- **An engineering team adopts AI coding tools, but reviewers struggle to verify the resulting changes. How would you build the missing capability?**
  - Applied scenario · Senior · 🧪 generated from job-posting themes
  - Tests: Whether enablement is tied to verification and ownership rather than tool usage counts.
- **Two product teams need shared AI infrastructure, but neither can spare an engineer. How would you establish ownership without creating an unstaffed platform promise?**
  - Applied scenario · Senior · 🧪 generated from job-posting themes
  - Tests: Whether you resolve capacity and accountability before creating a new team boundary.
